knowledge_point.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-3z &=4 \\ x+2y-6z &=8.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -6 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -6 & 8\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=0 \\ y-3z &=4.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=0 \\ y &=3z+4 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 3z+4 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+0z &=0 \\ x+2y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+0z &=0 \\ y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=0 \\ y &=0 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
